comments.author: @erdvilla
comments.text:
For examples on why airlines avoid high mountain ridges and plateaus, you can look at South America. All their flights from coast to coast get some of the craziest turbulence.
The smaller planes have it worse, and also the departure city makes a huge difference, planes going East takeoff closer to the Andes and have to either ascend by temporarily going North-South or even out into the Pacific and then turning East.
But in some routes the planes simply push it through and make their ascent straight between the mountain valleys and ridges, and that can result in some violent swings for the passengers, sudden drops and vibration.
